# Weredale House in the Sir George Williams student press, 1968–1971

Found 2026-09-07 by the download-and-grep sweep of the `rma-concordia-publications`
collection on the keyword "Weredale". Most Weredale matches in that collection are
the Westmount street address and are recorded as false positives in f_5421. **These
five are not.** They describe the institution.

Context windows taken from the `_djvu.txt` of each item; the texts were deleted after
extraction per the sweep method. OCR reproduced as found.

---

## The Georgian Vol. 32 No. 25, 11 December 1968

> There will be a collection of any good articles, books, and records, as well as art
> of Fine Art students, on Dec. 10th and 11th, in bins on the mez­zanine and 5th floor.
> An auc­tion will be held on Dec. 12th at 1:00 P.M. on the mezzanine. **The proceeds
> will go to start art classes for the Weredale Boys Orphonage.**

("Orphonage" is the OCR and may be the paper's own spelling.)

## The Paper, 13 January 1969 — the Volunteer Bureau

> Their basic require­ment is for students to give a bit of their free time to help out
> the many people and groups in Montreal that are not able to pay for assistance. The
> Bureau has co-ordinated the requests of such activities as the Unity Club, East End
> Boys Club as well as hospitals, indi­viduals and **Weredale Home**. Usually the
> requests are for tu­toring of children and young peo­ple.

## The Paper, 7 December 1970 — Radio Sir George's Christmas project

Four items in one issue. The descriptive one:

> Radio Sir George's Christmas Project is to make Christmas for the boys at **Weredale
> House** in Montreal. **Weredale is a home for orphaned boys and boys from broken
> homes between the ages of 9 to 18.** Radio Sir George is giving the boys a Christmas
> Party Dec. 11 and hope to be loaded with gifts from you… These gifts are to be new or
> nearly new, wrapped, and with the age of the boy indicated. **A secondary project is
> also underway to donate used, but in fairly good condition, sports equipment for
> Weredale's sport's program.** …badminton rackets, ping pong sets, hockey and football
> equipment — pads and old hockey or football sweaters, floor hockey sticks, nets,
> skates, toboggans and anything else you can think of.

> **There are over 200 boys at the home** and CRSG would like to be able to give each
> boy more than one gift, but they need your help.

> This Thursday at 3 p.m., CRSG, in cooperation with the Student Union will hold a
> bene­fit featuring **Danny Farmar and his Blues Band in the Alumni Auditorium**. All
> proceeds from the 2 hour long live show will go to the Weredale House party.
> Admission is 75¢.

> Council passed motions to give $500 to the International Christmas party to be held
> this Friday and **another $100 to Radio Sir George's party for the boys at Weredale
> House.**

The same issue reports a professor's phone being tapped under the War Measures Act,
which places it in the aftermath of the October Crisis of October 1970.

## The Paper, 25 January 1971 — the Volunteer Bureau again

> Societies such as the Ca­tholic Family and Children Ser­vices, The Family Service
> As­sociation of Montreal, The St. Kevins Boys Club, the Bene­dict Labour House,
> Dawson Boys Club, Mackay Centre for Deaf and Crippled Children, Meals on Wheels,
> **Weredale House**, The University Settlement Group, The Douglas Hospital, and **The
> Y.M.C.A.**

## The Paper, 8 February 1971 — the ESA budget

A line in the published Evening Students' Association budget:

> **Charity (Weredale House) 100.00 100.00 100.00**

The same table is reprinted in the issue of 15 February 1971. That is the same
document appearing twice, not a second source.

---

## Why these matter to this wiki

`wiki/connections/related-camps/camp-weredale.md` already carries two glimpses of
Weredale House from the university press — Loyola's *The Happening* of 11 March 1974
and Concordia's *FYI* of 7 October 1976 — with an explicit caution attached: the 1974
item is **Loyola's** volunteer bureau, "so it sits on the other half of the merger from
the SGW–YMCA material gathered elsewhere in this wiki."

**These five supply the Sir George Williams half**, and they run from 1968 to 1971,
five years earlier. The relationship was the same on both campuses and predates the
merger that created Concordia.

The 1970 item is the only contemporary description of Weredale House's size and
population this project holds: **over 200 boys, aged 9 to 18, orphans and boys from
broken homes, with a sports programme of its own.** That is the institution behind
Camp Weredale, described while the camp was running.
